acceptance_met: No partition is actively delivered to both owners during cooperative transfer: assign_committed now commits revoked partitions' delivered positions (auto-commit on) before the new assignment drops their state, so the next owner resumes after delivered work (src/group.rs). cooperative_transfer_commits_revoked_without_double_delivery proves the full two-member history: A delivers 6 records, revokes one partition with an OffsetCommit of 3, B resumes at 3, and no (partition, offset) is delivered by both.

Revoked and retained positions/pending records are handled separately and callbacks see the documented state: revoked partitions are committed then dropped; retained partitions keep positions and pending records; the on_rebalance/auto_commit docs state the ordering and the auto-commit-off contract (src/consumer.rs). The test asserts listener events ([], [p0,p1]) then ([revoked], []) and retained-partition resume at offset 3.

Member loss, static membership and max-poll expiry cannot commit undelivered work: max_poll_expiry_commits_only_delivered_position proves post-expiry commit() carries the delivered position (1), not the buffered cursor (3), after the heartbeat LeaveGroup with the poll-timeout reason; static_member_unsubscribe_then_commit_sends_no_offset_commit proves commit() after static-member loss sends no OffsetCommit (tests/consumer_close_commit.rs).

With auto-commit off, revoked partitions are still not committed at revoke time (documented on on_rebalance): the synchronous listener cannot await a commit, so the application must commit before the transfer to avoid replay. No API change in this card.
